svg.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: ehr-rwe-eln: one OMOP lake, seven modules, on AWS
svg.desc: Synthea patients and Athena vocabularies become an OMOP CDM v5.4 database: built in a staging Postgres on the laptop, published as Iceberg tables in S3 Tables, and read through Redshift Serverless. Data quality, target trial emulation, synthetic data releases, and a synthetic genotype study read it; the ELN bridge writes lab results into it with Claude; variant curation classifies the study's clinical panel. Module results live in Aurora, heavy jobs run as Fargate tasks, and the app, RWE Workbench, runs on ECS with Claude on Amazon Bedrock.
svg.text: Dashed boxes are outside the project. Open the SVG on its own and hover a box for what it does and why.

g.title: infra/terraform: bootstrap/ (state bucket), foundation/ (network, lake, Redshift, Aurora, budget, audit), app/ (ECR, ECS, CodeBuild, Fargate tasks, Guardrail, alarms). Public subnets only, no NAT gateway: each task gets a public IP.

The dashboards: data quality, target trials, ELN extraction, synthetic releases, and variant curation, plus the agent. No sign-in; /api/agent has a daily token limit and 10 calls an hour per address, and curator decisions are off in the demo.

a.title: One container serves the API under /api and the static Next.js frontend at /. ECS Express Mode builds the load balancer, HTTPS certificate, and URL. The image is built by CodeBuild and tagged with its git commit.

Claude through the Anthropic SDK's AnthropicBedrock client, with IAM credentials (SSO on the laptop, the task role on ECS); no API key. A Bedrock Guardrail checks every /api/agent call. Used by the agent, ELN extraction, and literature curation.
CodeBuild builds the app image and each Fargate task's image into its own ECR repository; task image tags are a hash of their Dockerfile and task script, and tags are immutable.
An AWS Budget on resources tagged project = ehr-rwe-eln, CloudWatch alarms (agent tokens, app errors, Bedrock errors, Guardrail interventions) to email, and CloudTrail.

App state and every module's results (dq, tte, eln, synth, curation), plus omop_stats, the precomputed concept counts the agent reads, so public calls never reach Redshift. Never holds OMOP. Pauses to zero when idle.
The OMOP CDM v5.4 tables as Apache Iceberg in an S3 table bucket, namespace cdm, in the Glue Data Catalog; Lake Formation grants each reader its tables.

Every OMOP reader goes through it, in SQL that also runs on the staging Postgres. Billed per second of compute, capped at 150 RPU-hours a month. A Data API session is billed until it ends, so RedshiftSession ends it when its block ends.

Heavy jobs leave the laptop: gwas (PLINK 2 and REGENIE), exomiser, lirical, bias (BIAS-2015), and synth (synthetic releases and their reports); monitor, the privacy checks, daily at 11:00 UTC; and bastion, the tunnel to Redshift. Billed only while a task runs. Genomics inputs and outputs are in the genomics bucket.

g.title: Scripts, the ETL's staging database, and the R and Hail containers. Nothing heavy runs in local Docker; the containers here are for R's and Hail's own toolchains.

a.title: The agent's four read-only tools for Claude Code, over stdio (agents/mcp_server.py, .mcp.json). Nothing serves MCP on the public demo.

Postgres 18 + pgvector 0.8.7 in Docker Compose, ports on 127.0.0.1. The ETL, cohorts, and the ELN bridge write OMOP here; publish_omop.py copies it to the lake and reconcile_lake.py checks every column. pytest uses ehr_rwe_eln_test.

R 4.6.1 and Java 21 with OHDSI HADES: DataQualityDashboard, CohortMethod, and TrialEmulation. scripts/hades.py starts the bastion task, opens a tunnel, and connects over JDBC with a one-hour IAM password.
Every build and analysis step is a script: uv run python scripts/<name>.py. The run_*.py scripts build an image if needed, start Fargate tasks, wait, and download the results.
Hail pins pandas below 3, PySpark 3.5, and Java 11, so it has its own image, built only on request. Reruns the GWAS and compares it with REGENIE's.

g.title: The cohort pipeline builds the OMOP tables every other module reads. The ELN bridge and the genomics panel write rows back into them.

a.title: Open-source synthetic patient generator. Seed and reference date are fixed, so the same arguments give the same people: 23,421 by default.
SNOMED, LOINC, RxNorm, CVX, and ICD10CM, plus Gender, Race, and Ethnicity. Downloaded under their own licenses and never committed.
Free-text lab notebook entries on 200 hypertension subjects, generated with the extraction each should produce. Default, hard, and adversarial entries (prompt injections included).

Claude on Bedrock through the Anthropic SDK's AnthropicBedrock client, with AWS credentials (SSO locally, the task role on ECS); no API key. ELN extraction calls it a few entries at a time; variant curation sends it passages that name a variant.
Synthea CSV to OMOP CDM v5.4, checked against OHDSI ETL-Synthea with every difference explained. Condition and drug eras, keys and indices, then cohorts built from YAML definitions.
Claude extracts samples and results into a Pydantic model, validated before anything is stored. Scored for precision and recall against the known answers.

The one OMOP database every module shares: person, visits, conditions, drugs, measurements, eras, cohorts, and the ELN's and the panel's rows. Built in the staging Postgres, published to the lake, read through Redshift.
The same samples and results as FHIR R4 resources, in data/eln/fhir_bundle.json, for systems that speak FHIR rather than OMOP.
OHDSI DataQualityDashboard 2.9.1 in R, in the hades container, against the lake: conformance, completeness, and plausibility checks (the Kahn framework), loaded into the dq schema.

Eligibility, strategies, time zero, and outcomes in YAML. Propensity score weights, weighted Kaplan-Meier risks, Cox hazard ratios, bootstrap intervals, and negative control outcomes, in Python; OHDSI CohortMethod and TrialEmulation in R as checks.

Differentially private releases from a Bayesian network, a DP-SGD autoencoder, MST, and AIM, an independent-columns baseline, and a 30% holdout to judge them against. Made and evaluated by the synth task; the monitor reruns the privacy checks daily.

5,000 adults on three simulated chromosomes, with an odds ratio of 1.4 planted on hypertension. A GWAS is checked against the planted effect. A clinical panel puts real ClinVar variants at their GRCh38 positions in the same people, and its carriers go back into OMOP as measurement rows.

Classifies the panel's variants with each gene's ClinGen expert panel thresholds, from gnomAD v4 frequencies and Ensembl VEP consequences, scored against ClinVar and ClinGen expert panels, and against BIAS-2015 as a baseline. Claude proposes literature evidence, every quote checked in code; HPO, Exomiser, and LIRICAL phenotype rankings add context; a curator decides on /curation/. Results in the curation schema.
Each run's checks, thresholds, and pass rates, shown at /dq/.
Attrition, balance, estimates, and negative controls for each protocol, shown at /tte/.
Each release with its provenance, fidelity, utility, trial parity, and privacy risk reports, plus a data card per release. Shown at /synth/.
Laid out as dbGaP distributes a study, in data/genomics and the genomics bucket, where the Fargate tasks read them. The registry linking study codes to persons is written apart, to data/registry/.
PLINK 2 QC and principal components, then REGENIE, as the gwas Fargate task. Hail reruns it and compares the results variant by variant.

g.title: What runs before code reaches main.

a.title: Lint, format, YAML, large-file, private-key, and gitleaks secret checks before a commit lands.
main is protected: every change arrives as a pull request, up to date with main, with lint-test, secrets, and terraform passing, and is squash-merged.

lint-test: uv sync --locked, ruff, and pytest against the same pgvector image as Compose. secrets: gitleaks over every commit and every file, for keys, tokens, passwords, usernames, and email addresses. terraform: fmt, validate, tflint, trivy.
Fast tests on small planted data, each in a rolled-back transaction in its own test database. Nothing leaves the machine.
Golden cases for the agent, ELN extraction, and literature evidence against Claude on Bedrock. Slow and billed, so never in CI.
